add.issue.name: Split source/mcp/epiq-api.ts (2.7k lines) into domain modules under source/mcp/api/

edit.description.md: `source/mcp/epiq-api.ts` is one flat 2,747-line module holding boot, boards, swimlanes, issues, tags, contributors, comments, attachments and the GUI state derivation. Split it along those seams into `source/mcp/api/*.ts`, with `epiq-api.ts` kept as a barrel so the ten importers (server, GUI api, tests) do not change. Pure move: no behaviour change, declaration bodies identical to the old file.

add.issue.name: Split gui/client/lib/scrubber.ts into a lib/scrubber/ directory, one module per question

edit.description.md: `source/gui/client/lib/scrubber.ts` (981 lines) answers eight unrelated questions: track layout constants, axis bucketing, event categories and identities, event dots, calendar segments, scope/period ranges, entrance animations, media-query hooks, and the board filter. Split into `lib/scrubber/<question>.ts` with `scrubber.ts` re-exporting, so its sixteen importers and the 1k-line test file keep working unchanged. Pure move.

add.issue.name: Split IssueCommits.tsx: diff-location URL helpers to lib, row components to their own files

edit.description.md: `components/IssueCommits.tsx` (1,193 lines) mixes URL-param helpers (`readDiffLocationParams`, `writeDiffLocationParams`, `CommitFocus`), snippet helpers (`extractSnippet`, `dedent`) and five components (`DiffStat`, `SelectionComposer`, `DiffCommentAnnotation`, `FileRow`, `CommitRow`, `IssueCommits`). Move the helpers to `lib/diff-location.ts` and `lib/snippet.ts`, the row components to their own component files, and point the four importers (App, IssueComments, IssueDetails, the test) at the new homes. Pure move.

add.issue.name: Move the inline TUI commands out of commands.ts into commands/*.cmd.ts

edit.description.md: `source/lib/command-line/commands.ts` (921 lines) already has the convention of one file per command under `commands/*.cmd.ts`, but nine commands (delete, close, reopen, rename, tag, untag, assign, unassign, comment) still live inline in the `commands` array, each 50–100 lines. Move them out following the existing pattern so `commands.ts` becomes the registry it was meant to be. Pure move; TUI behaviour unchanged.

add.issue.name: Split event-materialize.ts's handler map by domain

edit.description.md: `source/lib/event/event-materialize.ts` (1,067 lines) is mostly one 650-line `materializeHandlers` object covering 31 event types. Split the handlers by domain (nodes/structure, tags, contributors, issue lifecycle, comments, attachments) into `event/materialize/*.ts`, each exporting its slice of the map, and spread them together in `event-materialize.ts`. The replay/ordering logic stays where it is. Pure move; replay-equivalence and materialize suites are the gate.

add.issue.name: Extract App.tsx's issue mutations and swimlane modals into hooks

edit.description.md:
After 38G1FH7 `App.tsx` is still 2,055 lines with 24 `useState`s. Two seams remain that follow the same hook pattern as `use-board-socket` / `use-issue-detail`:

- the issue mutation handlers (`editIssueTitle` … `editIssueComment`, attachments upload/delete, ~450 lines of socket sends with error handling) → `lib/use-issue-mutations.ts`
- the swimlane create/rename/delete modal state and handlers → `lib/use-swimlane-editing.ts`

Hook order preserved; no behaviour change. GUI e2e suite is the gate.

add.issue.name: TUI and MCP each answer "who can be assigned" with their own code

edit.description.md: Found reviewing the split-giant-files branch (PR #246). `lib/command-line/commands/assignable-contributors.ts` (`getAssignableContributors`: registry names win, log authors are candidates too, `isExternal` for people who never authored) and `mcp/api/contributors.ts` (`mergeRegistryNames` + `getLatestNamesFromLog`, feeding `getBoardContributors` and `addIssueAssignee`) implement the same rule separately. Disagreement mints duplicate contributors for one person, so the rule should live once in `lib/` and both surfaces should call it. Not a pure move; needs a test that both surfaces produce the same candidate list.
